stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: PopInfo Weekly: Clarity, Carney, and corruption
stories.text: President Donald Trump amassed over $400 million through his super PAC, MAGA Inc. — the largest midterm war chest ever. Now, Trump has begun aggressively spending that money. Some ads inaccurately accuse Democratic candidates of supporting MAGA policies. Other ads, in an effort to find an effective attack, simply use false or fabricated claims. The crypto industry was desperate to pass the Clarity Act, which would legitimize and stabilize its business by providing it with a federal regulatory framework. Trump, who earned around $1.4 billion through his family’s crypto ventures in 2025, would be one of the primary beneficiaries of a permissive regulatory environment. On Monday, Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) released a new version that she claimed included more ethics requirements for Trump. But it does nothing to actually limit Trump’s business. ( UPDATE: The Senate saw through the ruse and blocked the bill from advancing on a 49-50 vote.) As the midterm elections approach, the AI industry has tapped a former Obama aide, Jay Carney, to build ties with Democrats. stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: The Quiet Corruption Behind Washington’s AI Inaction
stories.text: Political corruption is often perceived as transactional: Cash flows to a politician, who then proactively does something for a donor. But there is an equally pervasive kind of corruption that’s more difficult to see, because it isn’t necessarily in campaign finance reports that document the exchange of money. It is a corruption of inaction — and it may end up being the central force in our government’s decision to ignore the purported threat of tech billionaires’ artificial intelligence murdering us all. “Corruption of inaction” is a term invoked by Colorado’s Democratic Sen. Michael Bennet in our final episode of The Lever ’s new season of Master Plan — and you can see that stealthy form of corruption in both parties’ reaction to apocalyptic new warnings about AI’s dangers. The AI Crisis And The Corruption Of Inaction Donald Trump and the GOP offer the most obvious example: Bankrolled by tech oligarchs and personally invested in their AI technologies, Republicans are opposing the whole idea of new regulatory guardrails on AI technologies, which — by tech companies’ own admission — have gotten out of control. stories.title: Many of the “Michigan Jewish Dems” Backing Mike Rogers Are Actually Already Republican Supporters, Analysis Finds
stories.text: Story by Tom Perkins Over 400 alleged Michigan Jewish Democratic and independent voters signed a pledge in late August to vote for Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers, igniting a controversy and generating questions about whether Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed was losing critical support among a group that typically votes blue by about a 2:1 ratio. But a Drop Site review of signatories in the “ Michigan Jews Against Extremism ” campaign finds many of the Jewish community leaders involved have deep ties to the GOP, as well as to pro-Israel activist groups such as AIPAC. Nearly 50 were involved in a nearly identical gambit in 2012 that went by the name “Jews for Mitt.” Then-President Barack Obama, the group argued, was so “anti-Israel” that their consciences drove them to abandon the Democratic Party to support Republican nominee Mitt Romney. Among those who signed both the Romney and Rogers pledges are six members of the Schostaks, a politically powerful family behind a major Michigan development company. stories.title: The Curious Data Center “Gift” Haunting Ken Paxton’s AI Crackdown
stories.text: As he campaigns across the Lone Star State, Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton has seized upon Texans’ growing concern with artificial intelligence and adopted a hard-line stance, promising to crack down on rogue chatbots and rein in AI data centers’ tax breaks. His new “Texas First” AI plan calls for consumer electricity price protections, among other measures. But it leaves out that, as a state lawmaker, he faced fraud charges for pushing massive data center tax breaks benefiting a tech firm that had “gifted” him 100,000 shares. Also unmentioned: Paxton, now Texas Attorney General, holds up to $6.8 million worth of mutual funds invested in the data center or artificial intelligence boom — and his campaign has received at least $448,000 from other tech interests that stand to benefit from the AI build-out. “Ken Paxton has taken nearly half a million dollars from data center companies — that’s why he’s saying , ‘If we don’t have data centers, we’re going to be in trouble,’” Texas Democratic Senate candidate state Rep. stories.author: Ken Klippenstein
stories.title: The Mitch Is Back
stories.text: McConnell (R-KY) attends a Senate Agriculture Committee meeting on September 16, 2026 Fundraising fell off a cliff this summer. Not accepting a dime in corporate ad money allows me to be genuinely independent; but it also means I’m ENTIRELY dependent on readers like you to survive. Now God is responding in kind, casting McConnell as the villain in a sad sequel to The Mummy . The wheelchair-bound McConnell was hospitalized on June 14. His office said only that he was "receiving excellent care," and for the next two weeks that’s all we were told. Then on June 30 came the publication of a 911 call from his Washington home, in which a dispatcher reported a cardiac arrest and a medic radioed that CPR was in progress. Twelve days and a wave of public backlash later, McConnell’s office finally put out a statement. He'd only suffered a fall, they claimed, releasing the below proof-of-life photo. Note the newspaper on the bottom left to establish proof-of-life It took all of two days for the embarrassing display that Capitol Hill was surely dreading. At Wednesday's Senate Agriculture Committee markup of the Farm Bill, the clerk called McConnell's name and nobody could hear his answer. Sen.
